description: TerminaI documentation for Safety Architecture (TerminaI)
content: Safety Architecture (TerminaI) TerminaI’s safety model is built around one core split: Deterministic enforcement decides what review level is minimally required. The model/brain decides how to proceed safely (preview/plan/explain), but cannot lower the deterministic minimum. Invariants 1. Everything is possible with explicit user confirmation. The system should escalate review, not permanently block safety related actions. 2. Fail closed. If an action can’t be parsed/understood confidently, require higher review. 3. Minimum review cannot be downgraded by the model. The model may only increase caution. 4. Plain English consent. Before Level B/C actions, the user sees what will happen and why it’s risky (direct + indirect consequences). 5. Provenance aware. Untrusted sources can inform investigation but must not silently authorize execution. How it works When you approve a tool that modifies the file system (like or ), the CLI automatically creates a “checkpoint.” This checkpoint includes: 1.
